hierarchy: 3-level: gate(BLAZAR/OTHER) -> blazar_subgate(BLAZAR_HE/LE, direct fine passthrough) | nonblazar_router(5-way) -> level3 branch models
soft_routing_disclosure: End-to-end fine-class probabilities are a soft blend across gate -> {blazar_subgate | nonblazar_router} -> branch, weighted by each upstream stage's predicted probability, EXCEPT for a stage whose winning model exposes no predict_proba (the adaptive-LOO DecisionTree, the GPU Torch MLP, and the default probability=False SVM are the three such families in this pipeline's MODEL_SPECS) — that one stage falls back to a hard top-1 decision for that pass. See generalization_estimate.hard_routed_stages_oof above for exactly which stage(s), if any, fell back for the adopted configuration.
selection_bias_disclosure: Gate, blazar sub-gate, non-blazar router, branch, and (if adopted_combo != 'section4_6_baseline') whole-system configuration were all chosen by comparing validation scores across many candidates on the same data used to score them — a small, well-characterized optimism (Cawley & Talbot, 2010, JMLR 11:2079-2107) affecting these validation numbers, not any held-out test-set metric, since no test set is read anywhere in this file.
inference_note: Unassociated-source inference (fermi_inference.py) uses the same soft-probability gate/subgate/router/branch blend this file's chain-CV validates; the 3-level vs 2-level comparison on held-out test data is made by fermi_validation.py.
